# Trellis For Rust Consumers

Admin `Issuers.Rotate` generates private successor custody on Auth's host and
stores it in the private `<database-stem>.issuer-keys` directory (`platform.issuer-keys`
by default) beside Auth's persistent
SQLite database, not beside the potentially read-only provisioned seed. Back up
that directory with the database, original issuer seed and OAuth storage key.
The RPC returns the old-key-signed trust transition. Supply the expected current key ID
and an idempotency key; repeating the request does not rotate again. SDKs verify
the successor chain from pinned trust. OAuth storage custody is unchanged.

Console and the isolated OAuth listener require HTTPS outside explicit loopback
development. The HTTP insecure-origin allowlist does not relax that requirement.

Local runtime startup initializes protected administrator `admin` and returns a
one-time `adminAccountUrl` password-setup link unless an initial password was
supplied. Configure fresh credentials with startup `--admin-username`,
`--admin-password`, or `--admin-password-stdin`; explicit initialization is
`trellis init admin --config <path> --username admin` with optional `--password`
or `--password-stdin`. Links expire after five minutes. Until password setup, each
startup prints a fresh link and invalidates prior links. After setup, restart preserves
credentials; `--reset-admin` is explicit local recovery through the same account
flow. Ordinary RPC reset privileges do not authorize protected-admin recovery.

Generated service job handles and workers reconstruct retained lifecycle history
through the deployment-scoped runtime `Jobs.History` route automatically. Do not
grant raw shared JOBS-stream read permissions. History preserves original stream
sequences at a fixed upper watermark and uses the current service queue binding.
Detaching resources retains data. Explicit administrative deletion removes only
the selected detached allocation; shared streams and other queues remain intact.

Operator CLI: `trellis clients list|get|put|disable|delete` manages public OAuth
registrations, including exact loopback browser redirects.
Auth client flows are fixed on every Put: browser callbacks enable Authorization
Code + refresh; native without callbacks enables Device Code + refresh; native
with callbacks enables both + refresh. Adding/removing native callbacks updates
the supported flows. Kind is immutable; use a new client ID to switch kind.
Native HTTP loopback callbacks need no development flag; browser loopback does.
`put` reads generated AuthOAuthClientPutRequest JSON; mutations are revision-fenced. `trellis apis
list|get|review|accept|force-replace` uses generated Auth request JSON and reviewed
package evidence. Force replacement requires apis.forceReplace and explicit
breakage/consent acknowledgements. Console exposes OAuth clients and API catalog.

Identity-link approval remains a protected same-origin POST. Its no-store
continuation page shows a navigation link to a 60-second, one-use GET handoff
bound to the exact portal session, provider and account. Top-level navigation
reaches the verified IdP without relaxing form-action 'self' or leaking the
handoff in referrers. Direct, expired and replayed handoffs fail.

Own-context bootstrap signs the exact physical socket's broker `attachmentId`
and verifies its echoed signed registry ID; overlapping sockets never select
the newest attachment as a fallback.

Already admitted connections use `trellis.auth.metadata.get` for issuer-signed
public verification lookups, never administrative Authority.Status. Verify the
retained exchange and pinned issuer/rotation trust; broker delivery and missing
or unavailable responses cannot grant authority or clear known revocation.

Native service/device connections automatically publish the generated
Health.Heartbeat event through ordinary signed SessionEvent publication. Auth
assigns the runtime-only selfReport right during provisioning, not to users/apps.
The collector verifies catalog evidence, broker chronology, retirement cutoff
and signed native participant/deployment/instance identity. No extra service
contract declaration is needed; initial publication does not gate CONNECT.

Fresh administrator initialization grants explicit current Trellis-owned
Auth/Core/State/Health/Jobs/Events capabilities, not domain or future capabilities.
Console/CLI connections still require actual selected consent and client
privilege eligibility; administrator status is not blanket app authority.

OAuth CONNECT and authority/admission renewal consult the original verified
refresh family's absolute deadline and revocation state. Admission.Renew accepts
the live session-key proof and own context digest to return same-key admission
bounded by the candidate authority/family and 300 seconds; no refresh rotation
or durable reconnect credential is created. Provisioned admission must still be
signed locally by the client's identity key.

Use with [the consumer guide](llms-full.txt) from the same Trellis revision.
Trellis does not prescribe an application's configuration parser, database,
domain types, DI pattern, logging setup, or test framework.

## Generated Package

Revision 7 Auth signs and retains catalog snapshots, provider certificates,
monotonic issuer rotations, logical-session authority, and session revocations.
`trellis-protocol` authenticates these records against pinned instance/account
trust. Catalog membership checks also require verified live authority and its
retirement status; decoding a record is not trust. The Rust SDK consumes verified
OAuth sessions and proof-bearing provisioned CONNECT credentials through the
production host, CLI, and application transports.
Do not revive the retired GrantBinding/browser-bind protocol or install a watcher
per context as a compatibility path.

Native OAuth custody binds each credential handle to the selected issuer,
installation, NATS account, and client identity. Owner-only files retain the
persistent DPoP key and rotating refresh family; an operating-system lock spans
read, exchange, and commit across processes. Mark recovery before exchange so
a lost response cannot trigger replay of a spent refresh token. Platforms
without this owner-only adapter must supply an explicit secure-store adapter.
Native CLI and production Callout/startup paths use this custody implementation.

Cold OAuth resume verifies signed issuer successors from the retained pin using
GET /.well-known/trellis/issuer-chain at the selected OAuth origin and persists
successor trust before spending a refresh token. Unavailable or invalid chains
leave it unspent. A successfully returned new token survives later issuer
verification failure, but its admission remains unusable until authenticated.
Never retry an ambiguously spent predecessor.
Node-native and browser peers reuse admission only while shared verification accepts its
lifetime and current pinned trust; transport loss alone does not spend refresh
custody. Renewal checks the selected HTTP origin before spending the token. An
ambiguous token POST still requires explicit recovery, with no application-request
retransmission or revocation reset.
Store object deletion and replacement clean up chunks only in the admitted
identity's allocated Object Store streams, including Operation staging. This
does not authorize KV purge, stream destruction, or cross-owner Store access.

Live authority requires an applied initial revocation snapshot and current
coverage. Lost coverage makes retained handles unavailable until recovery;
epoch fencing prevents retired watchers from changing successor coverage.
Rust and TypeScript stage mirror rollover without stopping a healthy predecessor.
Its verified coverage protects retained work until authenticated replacement
replay completes; fresh application IO on the replacement remains fenced until
its checked snapshot is ready. Actual mirror loss remains unavailable, and known
revocations survive failure, cancellation, and replacement. Recovery never replays
application requests.

Native applications pass a verified `NativeOAuthSession` and explicit broker
endpoints to `UserConnectOptions::new(nats_servers, timeout_ms, session)`. The SDK
retains credential custody and renews admission with the same runtime identity
and key, using its owner's authenticated issuer pin. Recovery failure closes
application transport without deleting the durable credential record.

Explicitly initialized or administrator-registered loopback development clients
may receive eligible platform privileges through normal user authority and
explicit delegation. Registration requires clients.manage; configuring privilege
eligibility also requires privileges.manage. Localhost establishes no trust;
CIMD clients remain ineligible, and application/OAuth origins remain isolated.

Finite administrative privilege requests are explicit OAuth RAR selections,
separate from generated application capability requests. Native IDL does not
define privilege-request syntax, and selecting an administrative API capability
does not grant its additional finite privilege. Registration eligibility, user
authority, and explicit consent remain required even for optional requests.

Explicit one-off consent overrides older remembered choices without changing
them. Reused choices retain their expiry; later shared withdrawals still retire
affected sessions. A shortened effective authorization deadline is a reduction
unless another entitlement path preserves the outstanding authority.
Consent approval binds the current server-owned presentation and the selected
optional capabilities; stale forms require a fresh presentation. Signed session
authority has a shared 64 KiB issuer, verification, and parsing budget.
Provisional CIMD client intake shares a 128-client/16 MiB budget and a five-minute
lifetime; live decisions and approved refresh lifecycles are retained. Exhaustion
returns `temporarily_unavailable`, not administrative registration or authority.
Deadlines on newly gained rights bound new contexts, not older narrower contexts
or the logical-session root.

Revision 7's breaking routing cutover uses canonical generated API/action
subjects for RPC, Operation starts, and Live openings. Providers sharing a
logical API share request queues and must be suitable alternatives; identical
IDL does not make independent databases or physical devices interchangeable.
Signed provider identity, generation/action checks, and service-owned resources
remain separate from caller capabilities. Established Live/Transfer traffic
and existing Operation controls retain owner-directed routing. There is no
persisted caller-to-deployment selection or automatic retry of potentially
executed requests. This decision is still being integrated on this branch.

Complete serialized Operation references require `deploymentId`, verified against
certified signed acceptance. SDKs route get/watch/wait/cancel/signals to that
deployment and restore only complete references, never IDs alone. Replicas in
that deployment retain existing executor leases and CAS fencing. The reference
is routing metadata, not authority. Invocation deduplication is deployment-scoped;
an uncertain canonical start must not automatically retry into another deployment.
No cross-deployment idempotency is promised.

Provisioned services/devices prove possession of their identity key and a fresh
runtime/session key for the configured installation/account. Auth derives their
deployment, instance, participant, and implementation authority from current
provisioning records; clients never assert those bindings during CONNECT.
Provisioning still supplies broker endpoints and pinned installation/issuer trust.
Immediate ServiceInstances.Provision and Devices.Provision require identityPublicKey
from a client-owned Ed25519 key. Trellis never stores or returns its private seed.
Missing identityPublicKey returns identity_public_key_required without provisioning
or consuming the idempotency key. provisioningSecret is null; activation-token
provisioning is not implemented. CONNECT proves possession of the registered key.
ServiceInstances.Provision awaits the ordinary native resource producer before
success (empty declarations and KV supported; other declarations fail explicitly).
Retry the same request after broker failure; retained allocations are never destroyed.

Auth.Resources.List/Get include all allocation states, including detached, with
digest resourceId, ownerKind (user/deployment), ownerId, and explicit state.
Declaration omission and deployment Remove detach and retain resource data;
Disable preserves resource bindings but revokes sessions and denies admission.
Enable reuses retained bindings without reapplying the contract or recreating storage;
there is no automatic resource deletion. Compatible re-add reuses retained data.
Explicit admin Resources.Remove permanently deletes only the selected detached
owned KV at expectedRevision after checking its physical ownership marker. Retry
the same manual request after broker failure; startup never resumes deletion.
Removal execution is exclusively claimed and incarnation-fenced. Recreating a
deleted logical resource uses a fresh allocation and physical bucket, so delayed
deletion cannot touch replacement data; compatible reattachment keeps the original.
KV history/TTL reductions that could lose retained data are rejected.

Auth Connections.Opened/Closed/Kicked publish generated AuthSecurityEvent values
through the admitted Auth provider. Event IDs and occurrence times survive durable
outbox retries; consumers should identify attachments by attachmentId and logical
authority by authorizationSessionId, not retired connection/session-key fields.
An expired delivery claim alone does not stop Auth: stale workers cannot
acknowledge or reschedule the intent, which remains recoverable by its next owner.

Declare whole capabilities in native IDL, not individual RPC/event grants:
`required capability read;` is required and `capability export;` is optional.
Generated callers expose the selected actions. Check capability availability
before invoking an optional capability; selecting it does not mean it was approved.
Services/devices are deployable participants; apps/agents are application request
descriptors exported through the generated `apps` namespace.

Administrative Auth callers consume generated `trellis.auth@v1` actions and
request their narrow ordinary capabilities. Runtime authorization additionally
requires the applicable finite platform privilege; capability selection never
confers it. Own-authority/session maintenance uses fixed session rights.
Capability discovery does not grant authority, and capability groups are not
presets expanded into saved exact-action grants. API authors set positive
`consent_revision` values; Auth owns acceptance and action/membership introduction
counters.

Request verification checks caller grants against the caller's exact signed
catalog reference, independently of the provider's pinned implementation and
certificate. Compatible accepted revisions within one API generation need not
match; neither catalog grants additional rights to the other party.

Provider-owned events require an exact issuer-verified event-publish action in
the certificate bound to the signed native authority, deployment, instance,
implementation, API generation, and accepted action revision. They do not require
consumer capabilities. Delegated publication uses whole-capability membership;
provider certificates never grant RPC caller or event-consumption rights.

Generated Rust Event subscriptions verify original bytes and proof before decoding.
Core NATS requires live publisher authority; invalid publications are dropped
without ending a healthy stream. Current consumer authority remains enforced.
Durable consumers use the original broker timestamp. Targeted DLQ replay resolves
retained original bytes and `originalPublishedAt` through authenticated Events
inspection, even after source expiry; replay-envelope bytes cannot replace them.
Retained events require trusted original JetStream publication metadata as well
as a signed publisher timestamp. Both times must lie within the authority lease,
and both must precede an ordinary revocation cutoff. Read time
is not publication evidence. Current consumer read authority is separate from
historical publisher authenticity; service code does not supply its own verifier.
For certified publication, both timestamps must also lie within the provider
certificate's validity window.
Ordinary certificate expiry or issuer retirement does not invalidate authentic
retained publications, including cold replay. Compromised issuers remain unusable.

Author native IDL and set `[package]`, `[sources]`, and `[generate.rust].output`
in `trellis.toml`. `trellis generate` is offline after dependencies are
available in the global validated source-package cache. A durable `consumer`
requires a direct `trellis` source package dependency containing
`trellis.events@v1`; select and lock its version before generation.

The output is one ordinary crate at the source package version, with
`orders_trellis::apis::<api>`, `orders_trellis::participants::<participant>`, and
`orders_trellis::apps::<request>`
modules, not independent SDK or participant crates. Add an ordinary Cargo path
dependency, for example `orders-trellis = { path = "trellis" }`. The generated
crate declares the published runtime dependency matching the CLI. It has no
generator build script, repository-relative runtime paths, or runtime-path
config in `trellis.toml`. Use ordinary Cargo overrides when developing against a
local runtime. Generation does not modify the consumer's Cargo manifest.

Commit native IDL, manifests, and dependency locks, not disposable generated
implementations. Run `trellis install` before building project-local SDK consumers;
package generated code when distributing them. Trellis-owned Rust SDK and runtime
API crates generate their built-in bindings into Cargo `OUT_DIR` from published
build dependencies, without requiring the Trellis CLI in downstream builds.
Native source packages, not canonical API/participant JSON, are the publication
and evidence boundary. Explicit generation targets select only the named outputs.

An API SDK contains types and descriptors. The participant facade supplies the
connection boundary and only the declared caller/provider surfaces. Its
constants carry source-package/participant evidence; applications do not supply
digests to service bootstrap.

## Connection

Service facades export `connect` and `ServiceConnectOptions`. Supply broker
endpoints, pinned `RuntimeAuthorizationTrust`, and the provisioned identity seed.
Obtain trust from initialization or authenticated provisioning, never by trusting
an unsigned discovery response. Name and timeout are optional builders:

```rust
let mut service = connect(
    ServiceConnectOptions::new(nats_servers, runtime_trust, &identity_seed)
        .with_name("orders-service")
        .with_timeout_ms(10_000),
).await?;
```

Trellis resolves deployment/instance assignment, installed package/participant
evidence, exact authority, resources, signed context, and broker permissions
server-side. The CONNECT proof contains no caller-selected deployment or API.
Authorization state is process-memory-only and is refreshed
proactively as SDK-owned maintenance. Renewing unchanged transport authority
promotes context and routing credentials without replacing a healthy socket.
Newly approved authority is adopted automatically on a readied successor; safe
accepted work retains its receiving connection until it settles. No manual
transport-refresh API, upgrade notification, or context-store parameter exists.
Retain generated facades, still-bound resources, and job references across
handoffs. While own revocation coverage is unavailable, fresh application IO
either waits within its acquisition budget or reports unavailability. Guarded
registry maintenance restores coverage and wakes calls without requiring a new
socket. Watch migration keeps cached authority and existing leases, while actual
revocation, reduced authority, and hard deadlines remain fail-closed. Raw NATS
access is physical, not a logical generation-aware facade.

Register generated providers before `service.run().await`. The service lifecycle
supervises its request host and workers. `with_timeout_ms(...)` bounds
bootstrap, connect, and request operations.

Apps/agents acquire native OAuth admission through the selected authorization
origin. Pass the verified NativeOAuthSession to UserConnectOptions and retain
the SDK-owned credential custody for renewal and restart. Use authorization
code with PKCE or Device Code according to the registered native client's flow;
do not persist a bare session seed as a substitute for OAuth custody. Devices
retain their provisioned identity seed and use generated activation/connect
options. Neither lifecycle accepts a raw NATS URL/JWT or client-authored
assignment as authority. Treat authorization denial separately from invalid
login rather than starting a login loop.

The Rust CLI's owner-only files and operating-system lock do not depend on the
Node SDK, whose default OAuth custody is process-local memory and whose durable
custody is explicitly application-owned. Node native connection.close() awaits
asynchronous lease release before returning and reports release failures.

Provision without identityPublicKey for a one-use, server-assigned enrollment
secret. DeviceActivationOptions proves durable and ephemeral key possession;
Devices.Reviews.Get/Decide require its confirmation code and expected revision.
Accepted companion deployments register trellis.device.<deploymentId>.companion
without granting user authority. Declare Auth's deviceCompanionsManage capability
in the child request and obtain ordinary explicit native OAuth consent. Associate
using DeviceCompanions.Attach from that verified user connection, then drop the
setup client and resume the same credential handle. Supply its independent
UserConnectOptions via DeviceConnectOptions::with_companion. Signed assignment
must match the descriptor, native client and exact OAuth grant. Required children
must be present; optional children may be absent. DeviceCompanions.Revoke revokes
only the associated grant/families, preserving other grants, login and parent.
Removal permits the associated user or an administrator with current delegated
principals.manage. Removing the declaration rejects new and pending consent,
while existing independently consented grants retain ordinary refresh.

## Typed Surfaces

Use the participant's generated methods. Dependency aliases are accessors on
`client()`; owned provider registration is under `handle()`. For the tutorial's
`orders` alias selecting RPC `Orders.Create`, use the generated
`connected.client().orders().orders_create(...)` method. Its argument type comes
from the generated API crate; it need not share the authored model's name.

Exact method and model names come from the generated crate. Match generated
declared-error variants directly; transport and unknown remote failures remain
distinct. Operations expose generated invokers and typed references for start,
wait, progress/watch, and optional cancellation/transfer. Native no-responder
replies become `ServiceUnavailableError`, exposed through
`CallError::ServiceUnavailable` or `TrellisClientError::ServiceUnavailable`.
They indicate that the requested service is not currently reachable, including
during a restart; they are not malformed protocol offers or declared domain
errors. Persist a caller-selected ULID before
`start_with_invocation_id(id, &input)`; this is the durable operation ID,
recoverable through `control(complete_reference)` after acceptance. To cancel a reserved invocation that may not
yet be admitted, use `start_cancelled_with_invocation_id(id, &input)` with its
original input. It requires both Invoke and Cancel authority and atomically
retains cancellation intent before new handler entry. The returned reference
does not imply finished cleanup; explicitly `wait()` for the terminal result.
Normal replay never clears that intent; an existing terminal result is returned
unchanged.

For explicit pre-acceptance owner selection, persist deployment, invocation ULID,
and frozen input before sending. Generated invokers expose
`start_on_deployment_with_invocation_id(deployment_id, invocation_id, &input)`
and `start_cancelled_on_deployment_with_invocation_id(deployment_id,
invocation_id, &input)`. The latter requires Invoke and Cancel. Bound starts never
fall back to another deployment. Choosing a target after losing a canonical reply
does not recover its unknown owner; deduplication remains deployment-scoped.

Rust and Node replicas use one deployment-scoped Operation storage codec. This
pre-release persistence cutover does not migrate earlier records: retain existing
installations unchanged and use fresh development/test state. Unsupported records
fail visibly; the runtime never deletes or recreates them as empty state.

Live user tests use `TrellisTestRuntime::create_user`, explicit
`grant_user_capabilities(&user, Request::REQUIRED_CAPABILITIES)`, one
`register_native_application::<Request>("app")`, then independent
`login_native_application_as(&app, &user)` calls. `register_client_as` composes
registration and login. User handles expose no password, are runtime-owned, and
never auto-grant or regrant capabilities. `register_client` retains its existing
seeded-administrator convenience.

Rust schema-validation issue paths use JSON Pointer: an empty path is the root,
`/` is an empty-name property, and property names escape `~` as `~0` and `/` as
`~1`, including missing required fields.

Owned event publication uses generated publishers. Durable handlers use declared
Consumer resources; Trellis resolves durable identity, local concurrency, retry,
authority, and scoped Events DLQ/replay. Delivery may repeat, so choose a
side-effect strategy that handles duplicates. Subjects include the encoded
qualified API identity and base64url parameter tokens; the signed descriptor
binds the exact API, dotted event name, and parameter count. Success is
acknowledged only after the handler succeeds; exhaustion is not acknowledged,
and Events journals the broker max-deliveries advisory. Owned-Consumer inspection
and terminal replay reporting do not grant Replay/Dismiss. Manual replay uses the same handler and
a fresh retry budget without rewinding the original Consumer, and confirms
resolution before acknowledgement.

Jobs are private service queues. Use generated queue handles and cloneable
`jobs_client()` handles for submission from other handlers. Worker registration
and processing are supervised by the service lifecycle. Jobs expose durable
state, retries, progress, cooperative cancellation, and live updates. Delivery
progress acknowledgement is automatic. Waiting for keyed capacity extends the
current delivery and does not consume an attempt before handler entry.
`Jobs.Summary` computes all matching totals, groups, and statistics
independently of a `Jobs.Query` page. Job deadlines are creation-relative.
Omitted retry means five ordinary attempts with delays of 5s, 30s, 2m, and 10m;
explicit retry requires exactly one fewer positive ordered backoffs than total
attempts. Broker redelivery is unlimited. Before business work, inspect
`job.cancellation_token().reason()`: already-cancelled job handlers must
reconcile earlier side effects. Cleanup errors preserve redelivery; previously
started work reaches Expired or Dead only after successful cleanup.
Never-started expiration confirms terminal publication before releasing its
recovered key slot, without running the handler. Publication failure retains the
reservation; terminal redelivery reconciles remaining slots before
acknowledgement. Ordinary queues use Block, not an authored stale policy.
Coordinator fail-stale takeover preserves cleanup for a recovered owner with a
fresh fence and `JobCancellationReason::StaleAttempt`; only that owner settles
Stale, without mutating the replacement owner's slot. Ignored stale completions
are nonterminal diagnostics and retain redelivery until cleanup settles. A
never-started displaced reservation settles Pending to Stale without handler
execution.

Native lifecycle publication awaits JetStream acknowledgement. Typed live
updates remain transient and do not require a durable stream.

Execution state and attempts follow accepted lifecycle transitions in broker
stream-sequence order. Created initializes but cannot reopen a job. Diagnostics,
heartbeats, logs, and progress cannot override settlement or attempts. A valid
Retried opens a new run under the same ID without deleting history. Work retains
its original lifecycle sequence through broker source metadata. Old-run
deliveries are acknowledged without touching newer-run coordination. Deferred
work rereads lifecycle state before acquisition.

Stopping an RPC caller's wait does not undo work already accepted by the
service. Use explicit Operation cancellation for caller-visible business work.

Operation get, watch, signal, and cancel remain bound to the creator principal
plus participant across reconnects rather than to one session key. A durable
Operation's watcher is a separate live session: it reconciles the current
authoritative snapshot once its transport is ready, then yields ordered typed
transient updates and terminal state. Get and initial watcher snapshots expose
persisted state, not speculative handler state; a committed write may be visible
after its ACK is lost. Not-yet-delivered nonterminal snapshots
may be conflated, but transient updates are not silently dropped. Opening or
closing a watcher never starts, cancels, or completes the durable work.
Completed, failed, and cancelled records are immutable. Rust operation handlers
can clone `control.cancellation()` and observe `Requested`, `OwnershipLost`, or
`ServiceStopping` with `is_cancelled()`, `reason()`, or `cancelled().await`.
They must stop and join owned child work, including already-running
`spawn_blocking` closures, before returning from requested cancellation. A
healthy owner renews its lease and leaves cancellation nonterminal while cleanup
runs; the caller's `cancel()` resolves terminal `Cancelled` only after cleanup
and the fenced write. A cleanup handler error leaves cancellation nonterminal
for recovery. Recovered handlers enter with `Requested` already set and must
retry cleanup without starting new business work; return `Ok(())` only after
cleanup succeeds. External effects may still overlap across owner loss; use
idempotency or external fencing.

Live observations and Operation watchers are authorized live sessions negotiated
with bounded opening requests. The provider signs its offer and frames; control
responses bind the session ID, logical command sequence, and command hash, and
continued authority is rechecked from retained context rather than per-frame
network lookup. A session has protocol liveness and credit bounds, not a total
age or message cap. Closing returns a receipt whose remote-cleanup state is
complete, incomplete, or unconfirmed, and reconnect is an explicit new open
rather than a silent reopen.

## Resources And Atomicity

Use generated State, KV, Store, Consumer, and Job handles. State is one typed
value without key/TTL; KV is typed history; Store is raw bytes. State/KV direct
historical migration runs in SDK memory without write-on-read. Resolved binding
payloads and subjects are runtime internals.
First-time provisioning can resume an interrupted allocation. Missing previously
materialized consumers, KV/object stores, Job keyed coordination, or Operation
storage fail closed; retries must not replace lost durable state with empty data.
Restore coherent durable state before resuming affected execution.
Runtime Jobs/Events resource evidence uses authenticated `Auth.ResourceBindings.Query`
with separate kind-scoped read capabilities and current binding digests. Split
roles never read another role's SQLite database. This is a runtime-internal
boundary; application services continue using generated resource handles.
Identical deployment Apply retains current ready resource evidence. Changed or
unmaterialized resources remain unavailable until reconciled; repeated Apply
does not make stale materialization evidence current.

App State accessors register generated native-IDL schemas asynchronously:
`let (state, registration) = client.saved_resource("0", idempotency_key).await?;`
(accepted historical versions add `&Migrations`). Identical registration returns
the current revision. Changes require an explicit current registration revision;
handle RegistrationConflict without blind retry. A version's schema is immutable.
Registration and stored-value revisions are separate CAS tokens. State declarations
request native State read/write/delete capabilities; the shared authority owner
remains authoritative.
`let mut observation = state.watch().await?;` uses certified Live Watch.
`observation.next().await` returns `Option<Result<Option<StateValue<T>>, StateReadError>>`:
outer None ends observation; inner None means unwritten/deleted. Initial and later
snapshots migrate in memory using the read codec, without writeback. Use
`observation.close().await?` and `observation.closed().await`; drop also closes.
No automatic reopen or retry occurs after transport/authorization loss.
Device State Watch descriptors are generated from native IDL into the SDK;
State-only devices need no built-in API package dependency.

Generated cursor-paginated RPCs add lazy fallible page/item streams. Missing
`next_cursor` is the sole end signal; general keyset pagination does not promise
a snapshot.

`StoreResourceHandle::list_page` and file metadata listing are key-sorted keyset
pagination with opaque cursors bound to the prefix query. The limit defaults to
100 and must be at most 500. Desired resource capacities are sizing hints,
approved commitments define authority, and generated bindings expose observed
provider limits. Trellis does not adopt or destroy foreign-owned physical
resources.

Store readers/writers support bounded streaming through `write_from` and
`read_into`. Shared Store reads pull finite, byte-capped batches on demand and
verify chunk order/count, size, and SHA-256 before successful EOF. Partial output
is not a verified complete object. Paused reads recreate expired backend
consumers at the exact next chunk while the pinned connection and stored chunks
remain available. Reader drop starts owned cleanup on the creating Tokio runtime,
including cross-thread drops; cleanup retains the generation lease. Native
ObjectStore links are unsupported. Whole-buffer helpers consume the same reader
but retain the entire object in memory. Generated Operation
references upload bytes with `upload(body)`; lower-level operation builders
stream with `transfer_from(reader)` without a caller-supplied size or hash.
Trellis counts and hashes bytes while sending and verifies size and SHA-256 on
receipt. Transfer v2 uses bounded windowed one-way raw NATS DATA, not one RPC per
frame. Download destination writes and upload backend-reader consumption release
cumulative credit; credit is not persistence. Upload success awaits backend write
completion and durable Operation transfer commit, before handler execution.
Across language boundaries, an upload transport error is not proof of rollback;
resume the Operation to reconcile its durable result before retrying.
Streaming grants contain logical session identities and runtime subjects only,
never physical storage details. Transfers remain pinned through authority growth;
physical disconnect interrupts them, and interrupted uploads restart from zero.
TypeScript peers decode download RPC grants with the Result-returning
`decodeTransferGrant` helper backed by the same Rust/WASM wire parser. This is
structural decoding, not a substitute for the transfer runtime's authority checks.

Operation watch transfer progress may be coalesced, remains monotonic, and ends
with exact persisted `transferredBytes`; do not assume one event per frame.
Cancellation is authenticated; before commit it aborts staging, after commit it
cannot undo the committed object.

SDK HTTP connections and optional `telemetry-otlp` exporters preserve an
application-installed Rustls provider, otherwise use ring locally without
changing the process-wide provider, and verify certificates against platform
trust.

Enable `trellis-rs` feature `event-store-sqlite` for
`SqliteInboxStore`/`SqliteOutboxStore` or `event-store-postgres` for
`PostgresInboxStore`/`PostgresOutboxStore`; database-specific `EventStoreError`
variants follow the same features. Neither SQL driver is enabled by default.

Prepared events and SQL outbox stores allow event intents to participate in a
local SQL transaction. The application owns its transaction and migration
execution. KV outbox/inbox stores do not atomically commit unrelated database
writes. See `/guides/libraries/rust` and current Rustdoc for supported stores
and transaction APIs.

SQL outbox claims expire after 30 seconds and can be reclaimed. Pass the claimed
record to `mark_published`/`mark_failed`; false means ownership was superseded.
`dispatch_outbox_once` returns `ClaimLost` for superseded completion.
Publication can repeat after interruption, so the claim fence is not
exactly-once delivery. Current schema helpers do not upgrade pre-release
layouts; applications own migration of any retained older database.

## Test And Verify

Run generation and the consuming project's own Cargo checks. A real-runtime test
can launch a Rust service from a Node test using `@oatscenter/trellis-testkit`
and its `TrellisTestRuntime`, which automatically acquires exact-version
SHA-256-pinned CLI/server release archives and delegates configuration and
managed NATS to those production commands (no installed Trellis executables or
nsc prerequisite). Its host is stopped gracefully first; bounded process-group
cleanup also reclaims the managed broker if the host hangs or crashes. A Rust
test uses the published `trellis-testkit` crate, which links and runs the real
production runtime in-process, chooses loopback ports automatically, and returns
the existing SDK connection options so your generated service and app facades
connect normally. No CLI/server executable or Trellis source checkout is
required. NATS is a real child process: the bare builder defaults to the
verified pinned download (network on first use). Only the verified executable and
archive cache is shared (`TRELLIS_CACHE_DIR`, otherwise the platform cache), so
later runtimes can boot offline. Credentials, broker state, databases, PID files,
and logs remain sandbox-local. Set `TRELLIS_TEST_NATS_BIN`,
choose `NatsSource::Path`, or choose `NatsSource::PathLookup` for a prebuilt
broker. Runtime/bootstrap crates are registry-distributed implementation
dependencies, not supported service-author surfaces; a service repository uses
`trellis-rs` and `trellis-testkit` APIs.

Account actions use the generated Auth RPCs. PasswordReset.Create returns a
five-minute, one-use token for `/account/reset?token=...` on the OAuth origin;
completion checks Origin/CSRF, credential CAS, and the requester's original active
logical session/current accepted `principals.manage`, then revokes login/grant
families atomically with the credential change. Bootstrap administrators use local
recovery. IdentityLink.Create returns a five-minute portal URL for the current
user; completion requires that same signed-in user and fresh nonce/PKCE-verified
upstream OIDC. Provider changes and identities owned by another user are rejected.
Creation retries preserve the original response, not a new usable action.

Use `/api` to discover current Rustdoc and generated participant source for
project-specific APIs. Private Trellis workspace crates are not consumer
dependencies. Trellis's supported Rust toolchain is current stable.
Historical issuer keys are resolved through the existing issuer-signed metadata
exchange, authenticated by the active pinned issuer or its forward-verified
successor. Historical keys never advance live trust; compromised keys remain
unusable. A retired catalog signer does not invalidate an immutable catalog
referenced by current signed authority. Explicit native authority refresh uses
the scheduled renewal worker and awaits authenticated publication and coverage.

The `accountRead` capability covers account resolution, reading your current
session and signing out of the current login and its application sessions.
`Sessions.Me` and `Sessions.Logout` require normal selection and consent.

Native OAuth renewal leases the current maintenance transport after HTTP refresh,
and retains it through signer lookup and verified authority promotion. Replacing
the physical NATS generation does not pin renewal to the original socket.
If no safe native carrier survives, fresh admission may replace a missed retired
logical session under the same valid provisioned credential and pinned trust.
Removed permissions are not restored, and revoked roots or shutdown cannot recover.

Native providers finish accepted RPCs across ordinary authority promotion by
reacquiring a coherent current signing snapshot within one configured deadline.
Handlers are not redispatched; provider, issuer, expiry and revocation checks remain mandatory.
Accepted finite responses may outlive the opening caller context, but not their
request deadline. Current provider verification, known revocation, cancellation
and logical shutdown remain enforced; expired evidence cannot start new work.

Generated Operation keys are `<version-qualified API>:operation:<action>`, not
method aliases. `OperationRef::reference()` exposes the complete serializable
owner reference; restore it with the invoker's `control(reference)` without
starting another execution. Both SDKs verify the exact consumer binding in Live
offers. Operation updates carry operationId, sequence, timestamp and the unchanged
observed snapshot alongside the declared update payload.

OIDC role freshness follows the selected provider/subject identity, not merely
the user's latest login at that provider. Other linked identities cannot supply
or remove its roles; direct grants remain independent.

Native and Device Code authorization never inherits registered-browser implied
consent. Explicit requested-capability approval and Device Code confirmation are
still required for registered native clients.
